Across the lake would be a whole road trip, and this was more like backing out of the driveway. From just offshore, Jesus sat down and taught the people from the boat.

That's it, baker. Luke 5:3 says Jesus asked Simon to “put out a little from shore.” That's not across the lake, just a short push out from the edge. Then Jesus sat down in the boat and taught the people from there.
Teaches it is. Luke 5:3 says, “And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.” I bet Simon didn't expect his boat to turn into a stage while he was washing his nets. Same boat, brand new job.

Healing is a good guess, but it's not in this scene. Luke 5:3 says, “And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.” So the boat is a place to teach from, and the verse gives us teaching, plain and simple.

Lake and water everywhere, so I see why you reached for that one. But the text doesn't mention baptizing here. Luke 5:3 says, “And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.” The people get a teaching, and Simon gets a boat with a very important passenger.

explanations.answer: We worked hard all night and caught nothing
explanations.explanation: Yes, and Simon says it plainly: “we have worked hard all night without catching anything.” (Luke 5:5) You know that feeling when you clock out after a long shift with nothing to show for it? I bet Simon knew it well. Washing the nets was the last thing standing between him and a break.

explanations.answer: We sold our whole catch before sunrise
explanations.explanation: You can't sell what isn't in the nets. Simon says they caught nothing. Luke 5:5 has him say, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything.” So there was no catch to sell, only a lot of work.

explanations.answer: A storm kept us on shore all night
explanations.explanation: A storm would explain a rough night, but the text doesn't mention one. Simon says they were out working, not stuck on shore. In Luke 5:5 he tells Jesus, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything.”
That's the reason Simon gives. Luke 5:5 says, “But because You say so, I will let down the nets.” A whole night of nothing, and he still lets them down. I'd have asked for a long sit-down first.

explanations.answer: Because the fish move at daybreak
explanations.explanation: That sounds like fisherman talk, but the text gives no fish schedule. Simon's reason is in his own words: “But because You say so, I will let down the nets.” (Luke 5:5) The reason is Jesus' word, not the clock.

explanations.answer: Because his partners ask him to
explanations.explanation: The partners aren't asking him anything at this point. They show up later, when Simon's crew signals them for help (Luke 5:7). Simon gives his own reason in Luke 5:5: “But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”

Empty again would be a sad scene, but that's not what happens. Luke 5:6 says, “they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.” A whole night of nothing, then nets that can barely hold what's in them. That's about as far from empty as it gets.

Right, nothing like last night. Luke 5:6 says, “they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.” The same nets that came up empty are now tearing from the load. Imagine going from zero to that.

Partners it is. Luke 5:7 says, “they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them.” No group chat for this one, just a signal across the water. When the nets are tearing, you call the people you work with.
The text doesn't call them servants. Luke 5:7 says they “signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them.” These are working partners in the other boat, and they come over to help.

Neighbors would be handy, but that's not the word the text uses. Luke 5:7 says they “signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them.” The ones who come are the partners from the other boat.

Sink is right. Luke 5:7 says the partners “filled both boats so full that they began to sink.” That's like stuffing a cookie box until the lid won't close, except this time it's two boats and a lake. A pretty good problem to have after a night of nothing.
Drifting is what boats do on their own, but it's not what the text says. Luke 5:7 says they filled both boats “so full that they began to sink.” That's a lot of fish for two boats.
Spinning would be a wild ride, but the text goes another way. Luke 5:7 says they filled both boats “so full that they began to sink.” The weight of all those fish is the whole story here.

That's it. Luke 5:8 says, “When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees.” Two boats full of fish, and Simon ends up on the floor of the boat. Verse 8 is the first time the text calls him Simon Peter.
The call for help came earlier, in Luke 5:7, when they signaled their partners. In verse 8, Simon does something different. He “fell at Jesus’ knees.”

explanations.answer: He runs to tell the crowd
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't send Simon running anywhere. Luke 5:8 says, “When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees.” He stays right there in the boat with Jesus.

explanations.answer: Go away from me Lord because I'm a sinful man
explanations.explanation: That's what Simon says. In Luke 5:8 he says, “Go away from me, Lord,” and then, “for I am a sinful man.” I think this is a heavy moment, and he's saying it right after the catch. I'll let his words sit there.

explanations.answer: Stay with me Lord because I need Your help
explanations.explanation: Simon says the opposite. Luke 5:8 has him say, “Go away from me, Lord,” and then, “for I am a sinful man.” I think he's in a heavy moment, so I'll let his words stand.

explanations.answer: Teach me Lord how to find fish like that
explanations.explanation: Simon doesn't ask for fishing tips. Luke 5:8 records him saying, “Go away from me, Lord,” and then, “for I am a sinful man.” Those are the words the text gives us, and they come with him down at Jesus' knees.

Taxes don't come up in this scene. Luke 5:10 has Jesus say to Simon, “From now on you will catch men.” The next job in the text is catching men.
Boats are all over this scene, but nobody builds one. Luke 5:10 has Jesus tell Simon, “From now on you will catch men.” Simon's boat is already full enough.
